transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-04-09
- Start: 10:02 AM PT
- Duration: ~48 min (scheduled 45)
- Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lisa (Nimbus Head ML), Marcus (Nimbus Infra), Priya (Nimbus Security), Jonah (Product)

Summary: quick check-in on onboarding progress, access (VPC peering / credentials), early perf results from week 1, tuning plan (batching/KV cache), and next steps for full pilot bench. Transcript quality medium — some words garbled ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "VPC pairing").

Topics: onboarding status; infra access and VPC TODOs; week-1 benchmark highlights; tuning (batching/quantization) changes; security questions; next steps and scheduling.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
[00:07] Lisa: Lisa here.
[00:09] Marcus: Marcus on infra.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:13] Jonah: Jonah.
[00:16] Diego: Diego, Redwood SE. Samira: Great okay I'll kick off.

[01:02] Samira: Main agenda — we want to confirm you have access to the staging env, review the week one perf snapshot Marcus sent, and walk through Diego's tuning suggestions. Any new blockers?
[01:20] Marcus: Access wise we got the initial creds, but VPC peering stalled — our cloud team says the peering request failed because of overlapping CIDRs. We're sorting. Also need to open a few inbound ports for health checks.
[01:35] Diego: Right if peering is blocked we can do an SSH tunnel for the bench, but that adds noise to latency. Ideally we get peering for clean numbers.
[01:48] Lisa: We mostly care about p95 latency at 512 tokens and throughput for our background reranker. Cost is secondary but still in scope.

[03:10] Diego: Quick notes on week-1 bench — Redwood ran the baseline from your dataset: median token-latency ~14.2ms/token on the dedicated gpus, tail (p95) around 210ms for 512 token runs, throughput ~220 tokens/sec per GPU for the config used. There was some jitter when many concurrent sessions hit cache misses.
[03:45] Marcus: That aligns with what we saw — we had intermittent spikes up to 320ms, believe it's related to initial KV cache warming.
[04:02] Diego: Yep, KV cache warming — sometimes the transcripts show it as "K-V cash" in the logs, small transcription quirk — but it's the same. We recommended enabling prefix caching for common prompts and a small warmup job that primes the cache before business hours.
[04:28] Lisa: How invasive is prefix caching to prompt logic? Our product team worried about hallucination risk with cached prefixes.
[04:41] Diego: It's purely at the serving layer. We don't rewrite prompts, we just keep commonly requested KV entries so attention keys hit the cache. It shouldn't increase hallucinations but we can run a quality check by re-ranking with a smaller sample.

[06:00] Samira: On tuning we suggested two quick changes: reduce batch_wait_ms from 12 to 6 for low-latency routes, and enable dynamic batching with a soft cap at 32 tokens per batch for long-context flows. Diego, any caveats?
[06:20] Diego: That will reduce latency for smaller requests but might slightly lower overall throughput; for your reranker path which is latency sensitive, it's worth it. For bulk embedding path we keep larger batch sizes. Also suggested quantization 4-bit for dev bench — helps cost but we need to validate quality metrics (perplexity / exact-match on eval set).
[06:48] Marcus: Quantization concerns — our infra team needs to ensure the model variant matches runtime kernels. Diego, you mentioned a kernel mismatch earlier?
[06:58] Diego: Yes, if you pick a community build that hasn't been compiled with the newer fused-attn kernel we saw 15-20% latency regressions. We'll pin the runtime and share the exact build hash.

[09:30] Priya: Security check — we reviewed the initial docs, SOC 2 cat II is fine but we need clarification on KMS integration and whether keys can stay in our HSM. Also audit logs retention is important — 1 year minimum for us.
[09:50] Diego: For Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can do customer-managed keys via a cloud KMS. Audit logs retention configurable — default 90 days, enterprise add-on supports 365 days.
[10:08] Priya: Ok please send the audit retention spec in writing. Also need network diagrams for our GRC review.

[12:00] Samira: I'll follow up with SOC2/HSM notes and the network diagram.

[13:15] Jonah: Quick product question — we're testing reranker integration with a lambda pipeline; any recommended pattern?
[13:24] Diego: If latency is critical don't batch across async lambdas — instead warm a dedicated pool or use a long-lived connection (keep-alive) to reduce cold start. Also use streaming to cut perceived latency for UI.

[15:10] Samira: Back to perf numbers — Diego, can you remind the audience of the test matrix you ran?
[15:16] Diego: Sure: run A — single session 512 tokens, seq=512, 16 concurrent clients; run B — burst 128 token requests, 200 concurrent; run C — reranker flow with 4 candidate scoring in parallel. We measured median/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Bench notebooks and raw logs are in the shared folder (link dropped in chat).
[16:03] Marcus: We pulled the sheets. I see an anomaly on Run B around 14:10 PST where p95 jumped — traceroutes show a 40ms hop to the gateway at that window.
[16:17] Diego: Could be our load generator hitting a noisy neighbor — we'll correlate with infra metrics.

[18:00] Lisa: What about cost projections if we move to quantized models?
[18:07] Diego: Rough ballpark — 4-bit quant reduces token cost ~30-40% for generation-heavy loads, but you'll need to trade off slight degradation in some eval metrics. We'll compute projected monthly spend against your request rate and share a table.

[20:00] Samira: Items for the next bench — once VPC peering is done Marcus will run the peered bench with the updated batching settings Diego will push. Diego will also run a run with prefix caching enabled and a warmed cache.
[20:22] Marcus: I'll try to finish peering tomorrow but I need to confirm CIDR non-overlap; if not we'll do a temporary /24 for peering.

[22:10] Priya: On compliance, two asks: 1) send the KMS/HSM integration doc, 2) provide evidence of encrypted-in-transit and at-rest for the dedicated environment.
[22:26] Samira: Yep we'll send the KMS doc and an architecture blurb stating TLS, disk encryption and key management notes.

[25:00] Diego: Small note about observability — enable token-level tracing on a small subset of traffic so we can attribute slow tails to cache misses or kernel fallbacks; costs go up but it's invaluable for root cause.
[25:22] Lisa: Agreed do it for 1% of traffic.

[28:00] Jonah: Any blockers on SSO? We tried the SAML flow and the redirect URL seems to get 302 loop.
[28:12] Samira: That 302 loop usually means the entity ID mismatch — Diego can look at the SP metadata.
[28:20] Diego: I'll take that item — need the IdP metadata and a sample relayState.

[30:00] Samira: Recap and next steps — Marcus will confirm VPC/CIDR and open the ports (Action Marcus); Diego will push batching config and check SAML metadata; Samira will send perf spreadsheet, SOC2/KMS doc, and network diagram. Priya will review retention and compliance docs. We aim to run the peered bench week of 2025-04-21.

[31:40] Marcus: Timeline sounds good. One more question — are there any automatic fallback policies if a dedicated GPU pool is overloaded?
[31:52] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports automatic fallback routing to a compatible hosted variant (if allowed by the pilot contract) and rate-limit-based shedding. We'll share the routing policy doc.

[34:00] Lisa: For the QA run, can we pin a control set of prompts to evaluate hallucination or drift?
[34:09] Diego: Absolutely, provide a 200-sample prompt set and we'll run quality baseline on each tuning variant.

[36:10] Priya: One small nit — please ensure logs don't contain unredacted PII in the debug traces.
[36:20] Samira: Understood, we'll confirm redaction settings on the next doc.

[40:00] Samira: Alright thanks everyone. We'll push the items and reconvene after the next bench.
[40:10] Lisa: Thanks all.
[40:15] Jonah: Thanks.
[40:17] Diego: Thanks, bye.

- Diego: Review SAML metadata and debug 302 loop when provided
